Rules:
- One commitment per line.

- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.

# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economic Policy
The manifesto proposes economic recovery through renewable energy investment and home insulation programmes. Key measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding apprenticeships, introducing Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 per adult, and establishing closer trade relationships with Europe. The party proposes increased taxation on banks, tech companies, and oil/gas producers, while committing to reduce national debt as a share of GDP.

## Healthcare
The NHS plan centres on guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) by recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. Other commitments include guaranteed NHS dentist access for emergency care, mental health hubs in every community, 62-day cancer treatment guarantees, and free personal care in social care based on the Scottish model. A Royal College of Care Workers would be established alongside a £2/hour increase for care worker minimum wage.

## Education
Proposals include placing mental health professionals in all schools, above-inflation funding increases, tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, increased early years provision, reinstated maintenance grants for students, and £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants. Teacher recruitment would be addressed through independent pay reviews and funded training programmes.

## Housing and Planning
The target is 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes. Ten new garden cities are proposed. Measures include banning no-fault evictions, three-year default tenancies, abolishing residential leaseholds, and giving councils powers to end Right to Buy locally. A ten-year home energy upgrade programme would provide free insulation and heat pumps for low-income households.

## Environment and Energy
Targets include net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030. Sewage discharge would be addressed through water company reform, a Sewage Tax, and stronger regulation. Tree planting would increase to 60 million annually. A Clean Air Act based on WHO guidelines is proposed.

## Immigration and Asylum
The manifesto proposes scrapping the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establishing safe legal routes for refugees, reducing asylum processing times to three months, and allowing asylum seekers to work after three months. Work visa policy would move from the Home Office to relevant departments.

## Constitutional Reform
Electoral reform proposals include proportional representation via Single Transferable Vote for MPs and councillors, votes at 16, scrapping voter ID requirements, capping political donations, and reforming the House of Lords. The Ministerial Code would become legally binding.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase towards 2.5% of GDP with Army troop numbers restored to over 100,000. International development spending would return to 0.7% of national income. The party seeks closer EU relations through a four-stage roadmap, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership.
